UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio (Central Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners); Ley 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital).
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office may serve only as a supplementary correspondence address; the registered office (domicilio social) must be a physically real address within Spanish territory where the SL is effectively administered, per Article 9 of Ley 1/2010. For the ISIC 5222 customs-bonded truck fleet activity, the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) customs authorization (authorized economic operator status or bonded transport operator authorization under the Union Customs Code) requires verifiable operational premises, fleet records, GPS-seal infrastructure, and demonstrative commercial substance; therefore a purely virtual office is insufficient for this industry and will not satisfy the customs substance test.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (negative name certification) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (inscription of the deed); Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (definitive NIF); Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (statutory publication).

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Articles 4 and 33 (minimum share capital), Article 20 (incorporation deed), Article 21 (registration), Article 22 (BORME publication), Article 60 (full-paid capital requirement), Articles 209-211 and 215 (registered office and directors); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, RRM), Articles 135-145 and 324-328 (inscription and appeals); Ley 14/2013 (digital incorporation via CIRCE); Real Decreto 1427/1989 (registry tariff scale).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) granted before a Spanish Notary and filed as 'primera copia' for inscription in the company's hoja registral.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ stage_2_statutory_formation_and_corporate_governance

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000 under Article 4.2 LSC. The capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind at incorporation (Article 60 LSC); cash contributions must be deposited in a bank account opened in the company's name with an authorized Spanish credit institution and evidenced by a bank certificate (certificado de desembolso) delivered to the Notary. No separate escrow account is required by law; the deposit is released upon registration. Note: although the input metadata flags 'minimum_capital_requirement' as false, Spanish law is mandatory and no notary or registrar will form an SL with capital below EUR 3,000. For this bonded fleet entity, subscribed capital of EUR 3,100 is recommended, and the transport licensing regime separately supports this with a first-vehicle financial capacity requirement of EUR 9,000 under EU Regulation 1071/2009.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic offices at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; VAT-specific portal accessed via Sistemas de Información del IVA (SII) web services

E-government filing portal

For an SL in formation: (1) apply to AEAT for a provisional NIF (Form 036 or via notary) before executing the incorporation deed; (2) execute deed before a notary and register the SL in the Mercantile Registry; (3) file Form 036/037 to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF (9-character CIF format: alphabetic prefix, 8 digits, check digit); (4) register for VAT in the same censal census, obtaining the NIF-IVA (ES + 9 characters); (5) if making intra-Community supplies, also enroll in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) via Form 036; (6) non-resident shareholders need no local NIF for holding purposes but directors/representatives require an appointment-of-representative filing and, where applicable, an NIF-ES for the non-resident entity if it supplies goods/services, with all filings performed digitally using an electronic certificate (certificado digital/FNMT).

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation; Spanish tax-resident SLs are taxed on worldwide income in the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) at the standard 25% rate, with no pass-through attribution to shareholders; no check-the-box exists, and the SL is per se a corporation; branches of foreign entities are entity-level taxed on Spanish-source income with a 25% rate (spect the absence of territorial exemption), and the Canary Islands ZEC zone grants a reduced 4% IS rate and territorial concessions for qualifying operations but does not alter the Entity_Level_Taxation default classification. — For an SL in formation: (1) apply to AEAT for a provisional NIF (Form 036 or via notary) before executing the incorporation deed; (2) execute deed before a notary and register the SL in the Mercantile Registry; (3) file Form 036/037 to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF (9-character CIF format: alphabetic prefix, 8 digits, check digit); (4) register for VAT in the same censal census, obtaining the NIF-IVA (ES + 9 characters); (5) if making intra-Community supplies, also enroll in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) via Form 036; (6) non-resident shareholders need no local NIF for holding purposes but directors/representatives require an appointment-of-representative filing and, where applicable, an NIF-ES for the non-resident entity if it supplies goods/services, with all filings performed digitally using an electronic certificate (certificado digital/FNMT).

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation; Spanish tax-resident SLs are taxed on worldwide income in the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) at the standard 25% rate, with no pass-through attribution to shareholders; no check-the-box exists, and the SL is per se a corporation; branches of foreign entities are entity-level taxed on Spanish-source income with a 25% rate (spect the absence of territorial exemption), and the Canary Islands ZEC zone grants a reduced 4% IS rate and territorial concessions for qualifying operations but does not alter the Entity_Level_Taxation default classification.

Available election forms

No check-the-box election exists; available elections and optional regimes under national law: (a) reduced 15% IS rate for qualifying 'empresa emergente' startups (Law 28/2022) for the first two profitable periods (base capped); (b) optional consolidated tax group regime (art. 100 LIS) requiring 75%+ direct/indirect ownership, Spanish-resident parent and subsidiaries, filed with IS 311000/AEAT; (c) VAT group regime (Régimen especial de grupo de entidades) under art. 62 octies LIVA for wholly-owned VAT groups; (d) cash-basis VAT regime (Régimen de caja) for SMEs with turnover ≤ €2,000,000 invoicing other cash-basis taxpayers; (e) simplified VAT regime (Régimen simplificado) for enumerated small activities with turnover below €250,000/€125,000, elected annually; (f) anti-hybrid notifications under Law 5/2022 (ATAD 1 & 2) apply by default with no election; (g) optional Spanish GAAP 'método de integración' for currency translations are accounting elections not tax identity elections.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general economic-activity exemption threshold: any taxable person performing taxable supplies of goods or services in Spain must register (Form 036/037) before commencing activity. De minimis concessions are limited to (i) the simplified regime (turnover ≤ €250,000 in the prior year for listed activities) and (ii) cash-basis VAT (≤ €2,000,000), neither of which relieves the duty to become a registered VAT taxpayer. Non-established foreign suppliers effecting distance sales or 3PL/warehouse operations likewise register via Form 036 without turnover threshold, subject to the simplified one-stop-shop (OSS/IOSS) alternative for distance sales with applicable EU €10,000/€100,000 dispatch thresholds.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Zero-rated (exempt with credit) supplies: (a) definitive exports of goods dispatched outside the EU/ECTA (art. 21.1 LIVA) where the shipper obtains and preserves proof of exit within the statutory period; (b) intra-Community supplies (EDI) to a customer holding a valid NIF-IVA, recorded in the VIES register of operators, provided the supplier files periodic VIES (£303/390) and the goods physically move within the EU (art. 25 LIVA); (c) transport of goods to third countries or the Community, and ancillary services (loading/unloading, customs clearance, bonded warehousing) physically rendered in facilitation of an export/import movement (art. 23 LIVA) - the bond truck feeder service between an EU airport and a customs-sealed transit hub qualifies where the transport itinerary is to/from a third-country destination and is evidenced in the CMR/airwaybill; (d) services directly linked to exported goods recharged to the exporter (art. 22.2 LIVA) when consumed in Spain but occasioned by the export; (e) B2B services supplied to non-established customers are zero-rated by destination rule (reverse charge in the customer country) under art. 5?? place-of-supply rules; However, the zero-rating requires the exporter to be the owner of the transit operation, to have valid EORI/TIN for customs declarations, and to observe the strict documentary evidence required by art. 21.2/24 LIVA and the Tarifas for 'depósitos aduaneros' where goods are declared to the 'Régimen de tránsito externo'.

  • DUA - Documento Único Administrativo (Single Administrative Document) incorporating the electronic export declaration in the Sistema Aduanero (e.D.T./ABA/CTTI), including the EORI number and the corresponding conditional exit confirmations
  • Exit proof (Justificante de salida de las mercancías - Cédula de despacho / confirmación del Puesto de Inspección de Frontera, stating the date of actual dispatch from EU territory)
  • Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (Conocimiento de embarque or Master House Airwaybill) evidencing the goods' routing
  • CMR consignment note (Carta de Porte por Carretera) for the bonded truck fleet operations showing destination, cargo count, seal number and customs seals intact
  • T1/T2 transit declaration or internal transit document (e-MRN via NCTS) where the bonded movement is under Union transit
  • Commercial invoice (Factura comercial) aligning description, value and Incoterms with the DUA
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (Justificante de cobro / certificado bancario de remesa de entrada de divisas or SWIFT MT103 / NIGE code from Banco de España Foreign Transaction Reporting) demonstrating the export price has been collected
  • Bank/telex evidence of payment within the reputed six-month repatriation window; for foreign currency billing the exchange rate must match the DUA customs value

Mandatory e-invoicing for all entrepreneurs and professionals from 2025 (Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece'; private B2B obligation entered into force after implementing regulation is issued, with the public-sector Facturae e-invoicing regime already binding since 2015 for suppliers to Government). For large taxpayers (turnover > €6,000,000), real-time fiscal clearance via the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires, within 4 calendar days after the invoice becomes registrable (8 days inclusive of extension), transmission of structured VAT invoice/record data (Field-by-Field XML) using SOAP/Web Service APIs (G2G attachments: L0801-Facturas, L0901/B, etc.), and submittance of annual G4/G5 book-electronic records; SII entities cannot use the simplified ledger and must file monthly VIES. In addition, the Verifactu bill-validation system (RD 1007/2023) obliges billing software to produce one-way hash-chained records and, where integrated in the SII, marks invoices with a 'QR' stamp, while non-SII taxpayers must provide an 'end-to-end' XML verification mechanism and standard invoice metadata; failure to integrate e-invoicing APIs or keep Verifactu-compliant logic triggers VAT-invoice-issuance penalties (up to €1,000 per invoice, aggregate caps under LGT art. 200).

Failure to substantiate physical exit, compliance with customs seals (precinto), or preserved documentation within the prescription window (4 years general; 5 years where declarations omitted; up to 10 years for certain non-transparent offshore structures) triggers retrospective VAT recharacterization at 21% plus late-payment interest (3.75% recargo de apremio escalating to 5% + 2% surcharge after 12 months, and up to 20% additional charge where the assessment is administrative). Export fraud or 'falsa exportación' penalties: tax-infraction fines of 50%-150% of the VAT improperly zero-rated (art. 191/193 LGT), nonlinear for repeated conduct; documentary inaccuracy penalties up to €15,000 (art. 198 LGT) per omission; Mekong? separate customs infraction fines for illegal export (up to 3 x customs value and disqualifications). Criminal tax fraud (art. 305 CP) applies where defrauded VAT exceeds €120,000, with imprisonment and fines up to 6x the defrauded amount and removal of zero-rating plus recharge of VAT from customers (the exporter remains liable and is barred from issuing corrective credit notes). The AEAT also applies the 'loss of the right to deduction' and cumulative clawback of input VAT previously reclaimed for the goods/services underlying the false export, with a statutory obligation to notify changes in proofs (FAU/Exports under art. 21 LIVA, resolutions ESE).

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a Eurozone member state with full liberalization of both capital and current accounts under EU law. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted subject to 19% dividend withholding tax and CRS/FATCA reporting. Hurdles for non-EU owners include beneficial ownership verification and source-of-funds attestation.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Export receipts must be repatriated to a Spanish resident bank account within six months of shipment date. Mandatory conversion to EUR; commercial documentation required to evidence transaction nature.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Annual accounts, management report where applicable, and statutory audit report where applicable Accounts must be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, the usual filing deadline is 30 July. $0 USD Registry closure may begin after one year from the filing deadline, preventing registration of most company documents. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 and may reach EUR 300,000 for companies with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million.
Corporate income tax return, Form 200 Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. Tax payable may trigger late-filing surcharges of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay up to 12 months, and 15% thereafter, plus applicable interest.
Beneficial ownership declaration or confirmation accompanying annual accounts Filed with the annual accounts. Beneficial ownership information must also be updated promptly when ownership or control changes; the annual filing should confirm current information or report changes. $0 USD Incorrect, incomplete, or outdated beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry compliance issues, and potential sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation, including significant administrative fines.
Annual return deadline

Accounts must be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, the usual filing deadline is 30 July.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) under Ley 27/2014, Article 29.1

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, Ley 5/2004) on dividends distributed by the Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder not acting through a Spanish permanent establishment. 0% may apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the non-resident corporate shareholder holds at least 5% of the SL's capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period and meets substance conditions. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15% depending on shareholding and residence jurisdiction.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year SLs the deadline is 1 to 25 July. A non-calendar fiscal year ending on 31 March requires filing by 25 September, and so on.

Deadline: · Frequency:

1 to 20 April for the first quarter, 1 to 20 October for the second quarter, and 1 to 20 December for the third quarter. For non-calendar fiscal years, each instalment is due within 20 days after the quarter-end.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box [1] NIF / Identification Spanish tax identification number, legal name, corporate form SL, registered office, and registry data of the company. Use the SL's Spanish NIF. Non-resident parent references must not be used in this box; foreign shareholder details are reported in the annual information return Modelo 232 where relevant. Late filing triggers the Article 27 LGT extemporaneous surcharge: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. If the return shows zero amount due, a fixed penalty of EUR 200 typically applies; if the AEAT required the filing, Article 198 LGT penalties may reach EUR 20,000. Incorrect or incomplete returns may be penalised up to EUR 3,300 or 2% of the amount if misreported.
Box [3]-[4] Fiscal period start / end Exact dates of the corporate income tax period, which must correspond to the financial statements filed and the board's annual accounts approval. The period must coincide with the Spanish statutory accounts. A mismatch with the parent's consolidated period does not alter the Spanish filing obligation and may trigger automatic inspections. Late filing triggers the Article 27 LGT extemporaneous surcharge: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. If the return shows zero amount due, a fixed penalty of EUR 200 typically applies; if the AEAT required the filing, Article 198 LGT penalties may reach EUR 20,000. Incorrect or incomplete returns may be penalised up to EUR 3,300 or 2% of the amount if misreported.
Box [20] Net turnover (importe neto de la cifra de negocios) Gross invoicing for bonded road feeder services, customs seal operations, airport freight handling, and ancillary logistics, reduced by returns, discounts, and VAT (if any). All non-EUR amounts must be converted at the AEAT official annual exchange rate. Intra-group services invoiced to non-resident entities must be at arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation. Late filing triggers the Article 27 LGT extemporaneous surcharge: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. If the return shows zero amount due, a fixed penalty of EUR 200 typically applies; if the AEAT required the filing, Article 198 LGT penalties may reach EUR 20,000. Incorrect or incomplete returns may be penalised up to EUR 3,300 or 2% of the amount if misreported.
Box [65] Taxable base (base imponible) Accounting profit adjusted by permanent and temporary differences, prior-year loss offset, capitalisation reserve, and tax-free goodwill allocations. Expenses recharged by the non-resident parent, management fees, and royalty charges are taxable adjustments unless they meet the benefit, business purpose, and bookkeeping requirements of Article 15 LGT and transfer pricing rules. Late filing triggers the Article 27 LGT extemporaneous surcharge: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. If the return shows zero amount due, a fixed penalty of EUR 200 typically applies; if the AEAT required the filing, Article 198 LGT penalties may reach EUR 20,000. Incorrect or incomplete returns may be penalised up to EUR 3,300 or 2% of the amount if misreported.
Box [125] Tax payable / settlement (cuota íntegra / resultante) Final annual amount of IS after deductions, double-taxation reliefs, withholding taxes, and quarterly instalment payments. Treaty/DTA relief is not applied in this box by the Spanish company; withholding taxes and refunds for non-resident shareholders are handled separately under the IRNR procedure, supported by Form 296 and tax residence certificates. Late filing triggers the Article 27 LGT extemporaneous surcharge: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. If the return shows zero amount due, a fixed penalty of EUR 200 typically applies; if the AEAT required the filing, Article 198 LGT penalties may reach EUR 20,000. Incorrect or incomplete returns may be penalised up to EUR 3,300 or 2% of the amount if misreported.
Box [234] Accounting result (rdo. contable) Profit after tax, based on the financial statements of the immediately preceding completed fiscal year, adjusted for instalment purposes. The Spanish entity must use Spanish statutory accounting profit; eliminating foreign parent IFRS adjustments keeps the calculation procedurally valid. For failure to pay or late payment of Modelo 202 instalments, Article 27 LGT surcharge plus late interest applies. Failure to file may be penalised under Article 198 LGT with a minimum EUR 200 per form; inaccurate presentments may be sanctioned at 10% of the tax amount, subject to the provisions on voluntary correction.
Box [235] Deductions and incentives Tax credits, deductions for double taxation, bonus reductions, and any applicable new-company reduced-rate relief. Only credits available under Spanish law may be deducted; foreign tax credits from a non-resident parent cannot be flowed through the SL. For failure to pay or late payment of Modelo 202 instalments, Article 27 LGT surcharge plus late interest applies. Failure to file may be penalised under Article 198 LGT with a minimum EUR 200 per form; inaccurate presentments may be sanctioned at 10% of the tax amount, subject to the provisions on voluntary correction.
Box [240] Instalment taxable base Taxable base of the instalment calculated using the statutory percentage method (18% of adjusted accounting profit for 2024) or the discretion of the taxpayer in certain cases. For cross-border bonded trucking groups, the instalment must reflect intercompany thin capitalisation and TP adjustments already known at quarter-end. For failure to pay or late payment of Modelo 202 instalments, Article 27 LGT surcharge plus late interest applies. Failure to file may be penalised under Article 198 LGT with a minimum EUR 200 per form; inaccurate presentments may be sanctioned at 10% of the tax amount, subject to the provisions on voluntary correction.
Box [246] Total instalment to pay Resulting quarterly prepayment to the Spanish tax authority after reduction for withholding and other prepayments already paid by the SL. Instalment payments are credits against the annual Modelo 200 liability; they do not reduce obligations of non-resident shareholders in respect of Spanish WHT. For failure to pay or late payment of Modelo 202 instalments, Article 27 LGT surcharge plus late interest applies. Failure to file may be penalised under Article 198 LGT with a minimum EUR 200 per form; inaccurate presentments may be sanctioned at 10% of the tax amount, subject to the provisions on voluntary correction.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 10,000,000 net turnover for the Spanish Local File; the Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated net turnover exceeds EUR 45,000,000. De minimis exemptions apply to individual related-party transactions of less than EUR 250,000 per category and counterparty, provided the taxpayer does not meet the materiality threshold. In practice, a customs bonded truck fleet SL with non-resident parent recharges must prepare full TP documentation if its net turnover exceeds EUR 10 million or group consolidated revenues exceed EUR 45 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like the UAE or BVI. However, Spanish tax law applies a modified substance-over-form doctrine through the general anti-abuse rule (Article 15 LGT), the substance and business-purpose requirements of Article 13.2 LIS, CFC rules (Articles 100-108 LIS), beneficial-ownership requirements in DTAs, and the MLI's principal-purpose test. A Spanish SL operating GPS-sealed bonded trucks for airport freight must demonstrate operational management, physical premises, local employees, service contracts, transport licences, customs bonds, and business risk in Spain. Insufficient substance will trigger recharacterisation, denial of treaty benefits, deemed dividend treatment, and TP adjustments.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Under-Declaration

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the defrauded amount under Article 191 LGT, plus surcharge and late interest. If the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud under Article 305 of the Criminal Code carries imprisonment and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount. Amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 are aggravated and may lead to higher prison terms.

Director personal liability: Directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for tax debts caused by their negligent or intentional failure to comply (Article 42 LGT). Individual managers who approved falsified freight records can be indicted as participants in tax fraud, face embargo of personal assets, judicial travel bans, disqualification from running companies, and imprisonment.
Transfer Pricing / Intentional Base Erosion

Statutory sanction: Corporate income tax adjustment under Article 17-18 LIS with secondary adjustments on the repatriated excess. Penalties under Article 196 LGT for non-presentation or incorrect TP documentation range from EUR 1,500 to EUR 22,000 per data set. Incorrect valuation causing harm may trigger a penalty of 15%-35% of the tax base adjusted.

Director personal liability: Directors, finance officers, and TP signatories are personally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties derived from false TP documentation. Criminal liability may arise for facilitating tax fraud if the intercompany pricing is knowingly fictitious. Directors can also be subject to commercial disqualification under Article 241 LSC and travel restrictions in cross-border investigation proceedings.
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Shopping

Statutory sanction: Application of the Spanish GAAR (Article 15 LGT) to recharacterise the transactions; denial of DTA or EU Directive benefits under the principal-purpose test; additional assessment at the 25% IS rate plus penalty of 35% of the recharacterised tax base; possible dividend withholding of 19% on deemed constructive distributions.

Director personal liability: Directors who sign treaty-relief certificates knowing the entity lacks economic substance may be jointly liable for the entire deficiency. In criminal proceedings, they can be charged as aiding tax evasion or money laundering; imprisonment, personal fines, prohibitions on contracting with Spanish public authorities, and freezing orders are available legal outcomes.
AML / Money Laundering / Cash Smuggling

Statutory sanction: Spanish AML Law 10/2010 imposes fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious and very serious violations; proportional fines up to the value of the laundered assets are permitted. Criminal money laundering under Articles 301-304 Criminal Code carries imprisonment and fines per transaction. Customs fraud involving commercial bonded operations can additionally trigger seizure of trucks and disciplinary action on the customs licence.

Director personal liability: All directors and ultimate beneficial owners can be prosecuted as money laundering co-perpetrators, especially if the company lacks a named AML compliance officer and fails to adopt internal controls. Personal liability includes civil recovery of illicit proceeds, travel bans, confiscation of personal and corporate assets, disqualification from transport licensing, and imprisonment for up to six years per laundering operation.
Late Filing / Non-Filing of Corporate Returns

Statutory sanction: Extemporaneous surcharge under Article 27 LGT of 5%-20% plus late interest; fixed penalties under Article 198 LGT of EUR 200 per omitted form, rising to EUR 20,000 where the AEAT previously noticed the obligation; sanctions for not filing information returns of 20% of the amounts not disclosed, with a minimum EUR 300.

Director personal liability: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate liabilities and penalties if they knowingly failed to cause compliance. Persistent non-filing can be treated as criminal tax resistance, subject to fines and restraint measures; directors may also be barred from serving on any Spanish board until the debt is satisfied.
